suggestions: pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
optimized_sql:
SELECT i_item_id, i_item_desc, s_store_id, s_store_name,
       MAX(ss_net_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
       MAX(sr_net_loss) AS store_returns_loss,
       MAX(cs_net_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
FROM store_sales
INNER JOIN date_dim AS d1 ON d1.d_date_sk = store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk
INNER JOIN store ON store.s_store_sk = store_sales.ss_store_sk
INNER JOIN item ON item.i_item_sk = store_sales.ss_item_sk
INNER JOIN store_returns ON store_returns.sr_customer_sk = store_sales.ss_customer_sk
                       AND store_returns.sr_item_sk = store_sales.ss_item_sk
                       AND store_returns.sr_ticket_number = store_sales.ss_ticket_number
INNER JOIN date_dim AS d2 ON d2.d_date_sk = store_returns.sr_returned_date_sk
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT cs_bill_customer_sk AS cs_bill_customer_sk,
           cs_item_sk AS cs_item_sk,
           MAX(cs_net_profit) AS cs_net_profit
    FROM catalog_sales
    INNER JOIN date_dim AS d3 ON d3.d_date_sk = catalog_sales.cs_sold_date_sk
    WHERE catalog_sales.cs_sold_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk
      AND d3.d_year = 1999
      AND d3.d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10
    GROUP BY cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_item_sk
) AS cs_agg ON cs_agg.cs_bill_customer_sk = store_returns.sr_customer_sk
            AND cs_agg.cs_item_sk = store_returns.sr_item_sk
WHERE d1.d_date_sk = store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk
  AND d1.d_moy = 4
  AND d1.d_year = 1999
  AND store_returns.sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
  AND d2.d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10
  AND d2.d_year = 1999
GROUP BY i_item_id, i_item_desc, s_store_id, s_store_name
ORDER BY i_item_id, i_item_desc, s_store_id, s_store_name
LIMIT 100
